Thank you for the demo last week. Our security team asked for a concise package that confirms (a) all inference processing and logs for our tenant will remain in AWS eu-west-1, (b) details on VPC peering/private endpoint options, and (c) egress/internet breakout controls for failover. Can you send an attestation or a small evidence packet we can circulate internally (security + infra)? If possible, include a diagram showing peering, egress path, and where KMS/HSM keys are held.

Cheers,

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -07:00

Hi Maria — uploading the artifacts we discussed. Attached:
- redwood_eu_residency_statement_20260813.pdf (attestation that processing, KV cache, and logs for Aurelia tenant are pinned to eu-west-1 for your account unless you opt into cross-region replication)
- soc2-snapshot-2025.pdf (control summary; full report available under NDA)
- CAIQ-extract-hosting.csv (map of CAIQ questions we consider satisfied by our hosting controls)

Notes:
- Private deployments use a customer-managed VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. In both cases control plane interactions are over the private peering channel unless customer requests the managed control plane in their VPC (private control plane option).
- KMS: customer keys reside in their AWS KMS in eu-west-1 by default. If you request Redwood-managed keys, we split key material in HSMs with a geo-partitioned policy (audit traces attached).
- Egress: we surface explicit fallback egress options (local NAT + outbound allowlist) and a documented failover to a backup region with explicit customer consent. Audit logs show no cross-region data movement for your tenant in the last 90 days.

Attachments referenced in the packet:

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@aurelia.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: EU-only hosting evidence + VPC peering questions

Hi Maria — quick technical clarifications and attachments attached.

1) TGW compatibility: our PrivateLink and VPC peering options are compatible with TGW transit routing. We include a routing appendix for customers that shows the required route table entries and NACL rules. There is a small caveat: if you use cross-region TGW attachments (to extend peering beyond eu-west-1) that is considered customer-managed inter-region transit and we will not mirror logs outside eu-west-1 unless you explicitly ask for replication.

2) Metadata: billing tags and per-tenant usage metrics are retained and processed in eu-west-1. Aggregated metrics used for capacity planning (anonymized, rolled up) may be processed in our analytics cluster in us-east-1; we can provide a contract clause to prevent cross-border forwarding for your account.

Attached: vpc-privatelink-architecture-aug2026.png, redwood_eu_residency_statement_20260813.pdf (signed by Hannah, Director, Customer Security Programs), and a short peering runbook excerpt.

If that covers it, I can open a DocuSign envelope with the signed attestation and one contractual addendum preventing cross-border analytics for Aurelia.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
